title: Sandakphu by Land Rover or on Foot
meta_description: Should you ride a Maneybhanjan Land Rover to Sandakphu or walk the ridge? Costs, time, altitude, comfort and who each way suits, with a side-by-side table.
summary: Walking to Sandakphu takes three days, costs about ₹2,000–2,500 a day each for a pair, and lets your body adjust to 3,636 m. A Land Rover takes about four hours and costs ₹6,500–9,000 a vehicle for a round trip with a night. Ride if time is short or knees are weak; walk if you can.

sections.heading: Two ways up the same ridge
paras: Every Sandakphu trip starts at Maneybhanjan, and the first decision is how to get to the top. One way is to walk the ridge, about 31 km over three days, sleeping at Tumling and Kalipokhri on the way. The other is to climb into one of Maneybhanjan's old Land Rovers and ride the same distance on a steep cobbled track in about four hours, through Chitrey, Tumling, Gairibas and Kalipokhri.

Both reach the same summit and the same view. Both need a licensed guide inside Singalila National Park and the same park entry. And both end at Sandakphu's lodges, where a dorm bed or a twin room costs the same however you arrived. What differs is time, money, comfort, and how your body copes with going from about 2,150 m to 3,636 m. The guide rule, park fees and Land Rover rates are revised from time to time, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Side by side

sections.heading: The case for walking
paras: Walking is the way the ridge was meant to be seen. You climb through three bands of forest, from pine and tree rhododendron above Maneybhanjan to oak, magnolia and bamboo around Gairibas and fir and dwarf rhododendron near the top. You stop for tea at Chitrey and Meghma, sleep in family lodges with wood-stove dining rooms, and watch the Kanchenjunga range turn pink from Tumling on the first evening. By the time you reach Sandakphu, the view feels earned.

Walking is also safer for your body. Climbing 400–800 m a day and sleeping a little higher each night gives time to acclimatise, so most walkers sleep well at Sandakphu. It is not much more expensive per day than riding, because a lodge bed and dal-bhat cost the same either way, and a group of four sharing one guide can walk for about ₹1,600–2,200 each a day.

The cost is time. You need at least four days from Maneybhanjan and back, and five or more if you walk down too. And you need reasonable fitness: days of 5–7 hours with stiff climbs, especially the first hour to Chitrey and the climb from Gairibas to Kalipokhri.

sections.heading: The case for the Land Rover
paras: The Land Rover makes Sandakphu possible for people who could never spend three days walking: grandparents, small children, anyone with bad knees, and families on a long weekend from Kolkata. Leave Maneybhanjan by 8 or 9 am and you can be at Sandakphu by early afternoon, watch sunset, see sunrise and be back in Darjeeling the next evening.

It is also part of the story. Many of the vehicles are Series Land Rovers from the 1950s and 1960s, kept running by local mechanics, and riding one up the stone track is an experience in itself. The owners' association runs them on a rota at fixed rates, so you cannot choose a vehicle, but you do not need to bargain either.

The cost is per vehicle, about ₹6,500–9,000 for a round trip with one night and more for longer trips or a run on to Phalut. Six people pay roughly ₹1,100–1,500 each; two people pay ₹3,250–4,500 each. Ask at the Maneybhanjan counter whether other trekkers want to share.

sections.heading: The altitude problem with riding
paras: This is the part most people do not think about. A Land Rover lifts you about 1,500 m in a single morning, from Maneybhanjan to Sandakphu at 3,636 m. That is a fast gain, and a headache, poor sleep, nausea or loss of appetite on the first night are common. For most healthy people these symptoms are mild and pass by morning, but they can be serious, especially for people with heart or lung conditions, the elderly and small children.

If you ride, spend the night before in Darjeeling at about 2,050 m, not in Siliguri. Drink water steadily, skip alcohol, eat a light dinner and go to bed warm. Tell your guide at once if anyone has a severe headache that does not ease, vomiting, confusion or breathlessness at rest. The treatment is descent, and a Land Rover can bring you down. Consult a doctor before the trip about medication such as acetazolamide if you are worried.

sections.heading: A Land Rover day, hour by hour
paras: Many people picture the Land Rover trip as a quick drive. It is closer to a long, slow climb with stops. A typical day in season starts at the Maneybhanjan stand around 8 am, after the guide has paid park entry and the driver has tied bags and gas cylinders on the roof. The first hour grinds up in low gear past Chitrey and Meghma, with a stop for tea and a look back over the Darjeeling hills.

Around Tumling the views open toward Kanchenjunga, and most drivers pause again. The track then drops through the bamboo forest to Gairibas, where there may be an SSB check, before the steepest climb of the day to Kalipokhri. The last stretch past Bikheybhanjang to Sandakphu is rough and slow. Most vehicles arrive between noon and 2 pm, which leaves the afternoon to rest, drink water and walk gently around the summit before sunset.

sections.heading: The best of both
paras: Many of our friends mix the two, and we think the mixed plans are often the best value. These are the combinations we suggest most.
list: Walk up in three days and ride back down to Maneybhanjan in about three hours, saving the knee-jarring descent.
Ride to Tumling or Tonglu, then walk the best forest stretch via Gairibas to Kalipokhri and Sandakphu over two days.
Ride up and walk down via Gurdum to Srikhola and Rimbik; you still take the fast altitude gain on the way up, but you get a full day in the forest on the way down.
Start at Dhotrey and walk the 6 km forest trail to Tonglu, then continue on foot, a short and gentle way onto the ridge.
Walk the ridge to Phalut and come down via Gorkhey and Rammam, then take a jeep from Srikhola, the full walking trek with a road at the end.

sections.heading: Roads, rules and change
paras: The ridge is changing. Parts of the Maneybhanjan to Sandakphu track have been widened and paved in recent years, and a motor road from the Nepal side now reaches the upper ridge. There has been talk of restrictions on private vehicles inside the park and of changes to the Land Rover rota. None of this is fixed for long, so check current status before you travel, and ask your guide on the day whether any stretch is closed by snow, roadworks or new rules.

Whatever you choose, keep the Land Rovers in mind on the trail. If you are walking on the track and hear one coming, step to the uphill side and let it pass; the drivers know every bend and they are carrying more than tourists.

faqs.q: How long does the Land Rover take from Maneybhanjan to Sandakphu?
faqs.a: About 4 hours uphill, depending on traffic, stops and the condition of the track, and about 3 hours back down. The route covers roughly 31 km of steep cobbled and partly paved track via Chitrey, Tumling, Gairibas and Kalipokhri. Snow or roadworks can slow or close it, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I drive my own car to Sandakphu?
faqs.a: Generally no. Private and hired cars from the plains are not normally allowed on the Maneybhanjan to Sandakphu track, which is served by the local Land Rover owners' association on a rota. The road and the rules have been changing, with paving work and a motor road from the Nepal side, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How many people fit in a Sandakphu Land Rover?
faqs.a: Up to six passengers plus the driver, with bags tied on the roof. Your guide also rides along. The vehicle is priced per trip, about ₹6,500–9,000 for a round trip with one night, so a full vehicle of six brings the cost down to roughly ₹1,100–1,500 each. Ask at Maneybhanjan if others want to share.

faqs.q: Is it safe to go to Sandakphu by Land Rover with children or elderly parents?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if everyone is healthy, but take altitude seriously. The ride gains about 1,500 m in a morning, and headaches and poor sleep on the first night are common. Spend the night before in Darjeeling, drink water, keep everyone warm and descend if symptoms are severe. Consult a doctor first for anyone with heart or lung conditions.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide if I go to Sandakphu by Land Rover?
faqs.a: Yes. A licensed local guide is compulsory for every group entering Singalila National Park, whether you walk or ride. The guide rides in the Land Rover with you and arranges lodges at Sandakphu. Guide fees are about ₹1,500–2,000 a day per group. Check current status of the rule and fees before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I walk up and take a Land Rover down?
faqs.a: Yes, and many trekkers do. Walk up in three days via Tumling and Kalipokhri, then ride back to Maneybhanjan from Sandakphu in about three hours. Your guide can book a one-way vehicle, which costs less than a round trip. It saves your knees and a day, though you miss the descent through Srikhola or Phalut.

faqs.q: Is walking to Sandakphu cheaper than going by Land Rover?
faqs.a: Per day, walking is cheap, but the whole trip can cost more because it is longer. Two people walking four days spend roughly ₹10,000–14,000 each from Darjeeling. Six people riding up and back with one night spend roughly ₹3,500–5,500 each. For a pair, the Land Rover trip and a short walk cost similar amounts.

faqs.q: Are the Sandakphu Land Rovers really from the 1950s?
faqs.a: Many are. The Maneybhanjan fleet, usually put at around forty vehicles, includes Series Land Rovers built in the 1950s and 1960s, kept running with salvaged and hand-made parts by local mechanics. They were among the few vehicles that could manage the steep cobbled track, and the town kept them long after they vanished elsewhere.

faqs.q: Will I get altitude sickness going to Sandakphu by Land Rover?
faqs.a: Some people do. Rising about 1,500 m in a morning to 3,636 m often causes headache, nausea or poor sleep the first night. It is usually mild and eases by morning. Sleep in Darjeeling the night before, drink water, avoid alcohol and tell your guide about severe symptoms. Descent is the treatment.
